The doctor did a good job, but the queue management system wasn't as good as it should have been. Normally, when a patient is scheduled for dental appointments, there should be an appointment confirmation in advance. But here, there's "no …

Because we were short on time and our usual clinic was full, we came here instead because it's closer to home. After the check-up, they said I had 8 cavities and needed extensive work. So, I asked to go outside to discuss it with my foreign partner. A female dentist came out without any greeting. She explained the price, and it felt like I was being harassed. The point is, 6 months ago, we went to a dentist who graduated from America and has decades of experience, and they said my partner's mouth was perfectly fine. Six months ago, there shouldn't be that many cavities.

Actually, we only wanted a regular scaling. Before starting, the dentist told my partner that a deep cleaning would cost 2,500 baht for four different areas of the mouth. The funny thing is, we called the clinic and they quoted around 500-600 baht for anything beyond that. We kept asking if that was correct, and they repeatedly said 500-600 baht.

My partner told the dentist several times that he only wanted a regular scaling. The dentist finished very quickly, in 5 minutes. How can that be considered clean in 5 minutes? It seemed like the dentist was annoyed that she couldn't convince my partner to pay the extra cost. It was very unprofessional, especially since she had multiple appointments to attend to. I've been to several clinics for teeth cleaning, and they all offer fluoride treatments afterward. However, this clinic didn't do that. When it came time to pay, the bill was ridiculously high. They said there was a lot of tartar, but they cleaned very quickly for both me and my boyfriend. What kind of tartar problem is that? They charged an excessive price.

When I saw the price, I asked for an explanation of each step. They wanted me to transfer the money immediately and told me to wait because they needed to contact the clinic's owner/dentist. The dentist who performed the treatment kept saying they were wasting my time, and asked if it was because they hadn't received enough money yet.

Furthermore, I had to go back to get the filling fixed because I experienced severe tooth sensitivity. Even drinking normal-temperature water caused significant sensitivity. The dentist called their assistant into the room to witness my sensitivity, as if they didn't believe I was genuinely experiencing it. It was terrible. No normal person would lie about tooth sensitivity. I wasted money, time, and felt terrible about being treated this way.

I don't mind the money because I usually work abroad, but the service was awful and the staff were extremely rude. I do not recommend this clinic.

Is this what society has become? Everything is about money. What will the future of society be like?
